chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Khadija, who said:

Verily, Allah Mighty and Majestic sent down the Stone for Adam (peace be upon him) from Paradise, and the House (Ka'ba) was a white gem. Then Allah Mighty and Majestic raised it to the heavens, and its foundation remained.
And it (the heavenly House) is directly above this House; every day seventy thousand angels enter it, never returning to it again.
Then Allah Mighty and Majestic commanded Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them both) to construct the House upon its foundations.

key_terms.أُسُّهُ: Its foundation — the original base left behind when the heavenly Ka'ba was raised, upon which Ibrahim and Ismail later built
key_terms.الْبَيْتُ: The House — refers to the Ka'ba in Mecca, the physical direction of Muslim prayer and focus of Hajj pilgrimage
key_terms.الْحَجَرَ: The Stone — refers to al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Black Stone), a sacred relic set into the eastern corner of the Ka'ba
key_terms.الْقَوَاعِدِ: The foundations — the original sacred bases upon which the earthly Ka'ba was rebuilt by Ibrahim and Ismail
key_terms.بِحِيَالِ: Directly above/opposite — indicating the heavenly Ka'ba (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) is positioned directly above the earthly Ka'ba
key_terms.دُرَّةً بَيْضَاءَ: A white gem/pearl — describes the original luminous, pristine form of the Ka'ba before it was raised to the heavens

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the Ka'ba and the Black Stone according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted by Abu Khadija — a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) — provides a cosmological account of the sacred origins of the Ka'ba and the Black Stone. It describes that God originally sent down the Black Stone for Adam from Paradise, and the Ka'ba itself was a radiant white gem, before being raised to the heavens during some primordial event. The heavenly counterpart (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) continues to be visited by seventy thousand angels daily who never repeat their visit. The earthly Ka'ba was later rebuilt by Ibrahim and Ismail upon the preserved foundations, connecting this sacred site to a primordial, heavenly origin and affirming its unique status in Islamic cosmology.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin Aiz, from Abu Khadeeja,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent down the Stone unto Adam<sup>as</sup> from the Paradise, and (it is now at) the House (Kaaba), (and it used to) be a white gem. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majesti Raised it to the sky and there remained its foundation, and it is the site of this House (Kaaba).
Every day, seventy thousand Angels enter it, not returning to it, ever.
So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majesti Commanded Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> and Ismail<sup>as</sup> with the construction of the House upon its foundations’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Ahmad ibn ‘A’idh from abu Khadijah who, in a maqtu‘ manner has said the following: “

He (the Imam), has said that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, brought down the Stone for Adam from paradise. The House was a white diamond. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, took it to the heaven but its base remained, and it is the site of the House, wherein seventy thousand angels come every day and they never return to this site.
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, then commanded Ibrahim and Isma‘il, ‘Alayhima al-Salam,
and they built the House on the pillars (on that base).”’
